title: What to buy first and what later
summary: A sensible buying order for a beginner in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting: protection and comfort first, the gun only after lessons and a fitting.

body.html: A beginner does not need to buy everything at once. At the first lessons the ground or the coach usually lends you a gun, glasses, plugs and muffs. First find out whether you enjoy shooting, then buy gear step by step.

First, your own eye and ear protection. Glasses that fit well and plugs or muffs that feel comfortable are a matter of both hygiene and safety. To start, impact-resistant shooting glasses with an interchangeable lens and passive muffs or good earplugs are enough.
Second, comfortable closed shoes and clothes in layers that let you mount the gun freely. You probably already have most of this at home.

Third, a vest, as soon as you shoot regularly. For Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ choose a vest with the jacket line: a contrasting stripe 25 cm below the shoulder axis and parallel to it. Before you call for the target, and until the target appears, the top of the stock must stay below this line, and the referee checks it. The same vest works in Compak® Sporting, where no line is needed.

Later: the gun, a cartridge bag, a hard case, electronic muffs and extra lenses. Do not buy a gun before a few lessons: the coach will help you see which model and dimensions suit you and suggest a gun fit. More: Choosing your first gun.
Buying, storing and transporting a gun are governed by your country's law, so find out about licences in advance.
Do not chase expensive items: expensive gear does not replace lessons with a coach. Spend money on training and cartridges, and upgrade your gear once you know exactly what you need.

key_points.html: At the first lessons the ground usually lends you gear.
Buy your own eye and ear protection first.
Then comfortable shoes, clothing and a vest.
The gun only after a few lessons and a fitting.
Money spent on lessons often helps more than expensive gear.

did_you_know.html: Many grounds hire out guns, so a beginner can try several models before choosing their own.

quiz.q: What should a beginner buy first?

options.text: An expensive gun of their own
Their own eye and ear protection
A full set of coloured lenses

quiz.explain: Protection is needed from the first shot, and your own is more comfortable and hygienic.

quiz.q: When is it sensible to buy a gun?

options.text: After some lessons and a fitting
On the first day at the ground
Whenever a shop has a good sale

quiz.explain: The coach helps choose a model and dimensions, and the law tells you which licences you need.

quiz.q: Which vest works for both disciplines?

options.text: A vest with no pockets at all
A vest with the 25 cm jacket line
Any vest, as long as it is bright

quiz.explain: The line is needed in Sporting™ and does no harm in Compak® Sporting.
